statement: (i) Write down the first three non-zero terms in the expansion of $(1+x)^{1/2}$ in ascending powers of $x$, stating the range of validity. (ii) Use your expansion with $x=0.1$ to estimate $\\sqrt{1.1}$ and comment on the accuracy.
solution: (i) $(1+x)^{1/2}=1+\\frac{1}{2}x-\\frac{1}{8}x^{2}+\\frac{1}{16}x^{3}-\\dots$ valid for $|x|<1$. (ii) With $x=0.1$: $1+0.05-0.00125=1.04875$. The true value is $\\sqrt{1.1}\\approx 1.048808$, so the error is about $6\\times10^{-5}$ (the next term $+\\frac{1}{16}(0.1)^{3}=6.25\\times10^{-5}$ explains most of it).
hints: Use the generalized binomial coefficient for exponent $1/2$.
Substitute $x=0.1$ and compare with the true root.
